Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS : 2694 . 1963 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
SCHOOL CHALKS, MOULDED, WHITE 

0. FOREWORD 

0*1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards 
Institution on 26 November 1963, after the draft finalized by the Inks 
and Allied Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the 
Chemical Division C^ouncil. 

0.2 An Indian Standard on school chalks will ensure satisfactory quality 
of school chalks and would be valuably to those concerned with the 
purchasing of equipment for schools, 

0,3 This standard while prescribes such requirements as would ensure 
satisfactory quality of school chalks, it is necessary to mention that 
different results may be obtained on different blackboard surfaces. It is, 
tlicrcforc^ suggested that chalks complying with the requirements of this 
standard may be tried on the surfaces on which they are to be used 
before making a final choice. 

0,4 For size grading IS Sieves conforming to IS : 460-1962 Specification 
for Test Sieves {Revised) arc specified. Where these sieves are not 
available, other equivalent standard sieves as judged by the aperture may 
be used. 

0*5 Wherever a reference to any Indian Standard appears in this 
specification, it shall be taken as a reference to the latest version of 
the standard. 

0.6 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of 
this standard is complied with» the final value, observed or calculated, 
expressing the result of a tesi- or analysis shall be rounded off in accor- 
dance with IS : 2-1960 Rules for Rounding Off Numerical Values 
{Revised). The number of significant places retained in the rounded 
off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this 
standard. 

0,7 This standard is intended chiefly to cover the technical provisions 
relating to the material, and it docs not include all the necessaiy provi- 
sions of a contract. 



rs : 2694 - 1963 

1. SCOPE 

IJ This standard specifies the requirements, methods of sampling and 
tests for moulded white school chalks intended primarily for writing 
on blackboards. 

2. REQUIREMENTS 

2.1 Materials — Chalks shall be made from good quality caldncd 
gypsum reasonably free from poisonous and toxic materials injurious 
to human beings. They shall be of homogeneous mass frdc from grease, 
grit and sandy abrasives. 

2J1 Finish — Chalks shall be circular in cross-section and tapered at one 
end, and shall be of smooth uniform shape and size. They shall be 
free from external blow holes. 

23 Hardness ~ Chalks shall also produce freely, without scratching 
or otherwise harming the blackboards, visible and distinct marks that 
can be easily erased with a piece of dry cloth. 

2,4 Chalks shall also conform to the requirements given in Table I when 
tested according to the methods prescribed in Appendix A, Reference 
to the relevant clauses of Appendix A is given in col 4 of the table.

3. PACKING AND PACKAGING 

3.1 Chalks shall be packed in suitable paperboard containers which offer 
adequate protection to the chalks during transportation. Chalks shall 



IS : 2694 - 1963 

be tightly packed in the container and saw dust or other cushioning 
materials shall be used to fill up the empty spaces to prevent breakage. 
Unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and supplier, each 
box shall contain 100 chalks. 

4. MARKING 

4A AH packages shall be marked on the outside with the following 
information: 

a) Name of the material; 

b) Number of chalks in the box; 

c) Manufacturer's name or recognized trade-marks, if any ; and 

d) Identification mark in code or otherwise to enable the lot of 
manufacture to be traced from records. 

4.L1 The {Mckages may also be marked with the ISI Certification 
Mark. 

Note — The use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the 
Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regulations 
made thereunder. The ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard 
conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements 
of chat standard under a wcli-dcfincd sy^trm of inspection ^ testing and quality control 
which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer. ISI marked 
products arc also continuously checked by ISI for conformity to that standard as a 
further safeguard. Details oi conditions under which a licence for the use of the ISI 
Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors^ may be obtained 
from the Indian Standards Institution. 



5. SAMPLING 

5.1 Representative samples of the material shall be drawn and adjudged 
as prescribed in Appendix B. 

APPENDIX A 

( Clause lA ) 

TESTS FOR SCHOQX. CHALKS, MOULDED, WHITE 

A-1, DETERMINATION OF CALCIUM SULPHATE CONTENT 
A-1.1 Reagents 

A-Ll.l Quality of "Reagents — Pure chemicals and distilled water 
[set IS : 1070-1960 Specification for Water, Distilled Quality ( Revised) ] 
shall be used in the test. 

Note*— * Pure chemicals * thaH meAn chemicaU that do not contain impurities 
which affect the rasulta of analyeia. 



IS : 2694 * 1963 

A-1.1.2 Ammonium Acetate Solution — Dissolve 454 g of ammonium 
acciaie in two litres of waicr. Add ammonium hydroxide to make the 
solution distinctly ammoniacal. 

A-1.1.3 Diatomaceous Silica ~ Wash kiesclguhr free from soluble 
matter and dry to constant weight at JOS'* to ne'e, 

A-1J*4 Ammonium Hydroxide — 20 percent {wjwj. 

A-1.1.5 Ammonium IVash Solution — Dilute 100 ml of ammonium 
hydroxide to one litre with water. 

A^t.2 Procedure — Grind the sample in a mortar so as to pass through 
250-micron IS Sieve. Place about 4 g of the sample, accurately weigh- 
til, in a 600-ml beaker. Add 350 ml of ammonium acetate solution 
stifling the mixture thoroughly so as to lf>oscn the matter from the 
hottnm of the beaker. Add about 0*2 g of diatomaceous silica, accu* 
lately weighed, to the mixture and heat at 70 C on a steam*bath for 
30 ininiitcs with frequent stirring. Keep the solvent distinctly ammo* 
niacal during this period by adding ammonium hydroxide, if necessary. 
f ilu;r the mixture through a weighed Gooch crucible applying suction> 
il iiccrssary. Stir frequently to keep the diatomaceous earth suspended in 
i]ir li(|uid. Wash the residue with five 10-ml portions of hot ammonium 
aotaic solution, draining thoroughly each washing- Repeat washing 
ui(h cii^^ht 10-ml portions of ammonia wash solution. Dry the 
(iticiblc in an oven at 70X to constant weight. 

/ 

A-1.3 Calculation 

Calcium sulphate, percent A -^ (B — C) 
by weight « <^ ^ M 

where 

A = weight in g of the material taken for the test, 

B = final weight in g of the crucible and the contents after 
drying, 

C — initial weight in g of the crucible plus weight in g ofdia* 
tomaceous silica used as filter aid, and 

M = percentage of free moisture ( see A-2.2 f. 

A*2, DETERMINATION OF FREE MOISTURE 

A-2.I Procedure — Grind in a mortar about four chalks so as to pass 
through 100-mm IS Sieve. Weigh accurately about 10 g of the ground 



IS : 2694 - 1963 

sample and spread it in a thin layer in a pctri dish. Place it in an oven 
maintained at 100" ± 2'C till constant weight is obtained.

where 

A « weight in g or the ground material ukcn for the test, and

A.3. MEASUREMENT OF LENGTH AND DIAMETER 

A-3.I Procedure — Measure the length and diameter at two ends of only 
full length chalk by means of calipers and a foot-rule calibrated m 
millimetres or with a sliding caliper gauge. 

A-4. DETERMINATION OF WEIGHT 

A-4.1 Procedure — Weigh 10 chalks, drawn from the same box ( see B-2.2) 
at a time and compute the weight per tOO chalks for each box. 

A-4.1.1 The weight computed for each box selected for tests ( see B-2.2) 
shall not differ by more than 2 percent from the average. 

A-5. DETERMINATION OF TRANSVERSE BREAKING STRENGTH 

A-5.1 Apparatus — The apparatus as shown in Fig. 1 shall be of such 
construction that a slick of chalk can be supported at two points 63 mm 

WEIGHT PLA7F0PM 

iOAOlNG ANVfl.

FlO. I APfAaATW *0» DKTKKKUrATIOK OF TBAMBVERSS BbEAKINO STHPKOTa

apart, and weight applied by means of a loading anvil midway between 
the two supports and at right angles to the chalk. The assembly con- 
sisting of the loading anvil, spindle, and weight platform, shall weigh 
approximately 500 g. The weight shall be applied either by the use 
of lead shot or by the use of weights. 

A-5.2 Procednre — Before testing, dry the chalks for a period of 24 hours 
at 38** ± yC to ensure that they are completely dry. Place the chalk 
in position on the two supporting points so that the central axis of 
the chalks is horizontal. Then lower the loadii^ anvil carefully vntil 
it rests on the chalk in the middle. Add one by one suitable weights 
carefully to the weight platform until the chalk breaks. The transverse 
breaking strength of the chalk shall be the sum of the weights of the 
loading anvil, spindle, weight platform, and any additional weights on 
the weight platform. 

APPENDIX B- 

(Clause 5.1) 

SAMPLING OF SCHOOL CHALKS* MOULDED, WHITE 
B-l. GENERAL PRECAUTIONS 

B-l»l Samples shall be drawn from originally unopened and undamaged 

boxes, 

B-h2 Samples shall be protected from abnormal exposure to heat, and 
shall not be allowed to come in contact with any liquid. 

B-1.3 Samples shall be handled as little as possible, and contact with 
wet or sweated hands shall be avoided. « 

B-2. SCALE OF SAMPLING 

8*2.1 Lot — In any consignment, all boxes of school chalks drawn 
from a single batch of manufacture shall constitute a lot. If the consign- 
ment is declared or known to consist of different batches of manufa* 
cture, the boxes belonging to the same batch shall be grouped together 
and each such group shall constitute a separate lot. 

B*2.2 For ascertaining the conformity of the lot to the requirements of 
the specification, tests shall be carried out for each lot separately. The 
number of boxes to be selected from lots of different sizes shall be in 
accordance with Table IL From each selected box, 10 chalks shall 
be picked up at random.

B-3. NUMBER OF TESTS AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 

B*3.1 All the chalks selected according to B-2.Z shall be examined 
for finish ( see 2.2 ) and hardness ( see 23 ) If the number of defectives 
found is equal to or less than the corresponding number given in 
col 4 of Table 11, the lot shall be declared as conforming to the specifica- 
(tioii requirements in 2.2 and 2.3. 

B-3^ All the chalks selected according to B-2*2 shall then be examined 
for length of the stick and diameter at the two ends. Any chalk failing 
to meet the requirement of cithtr length or diameter shall be considered 
as a dcfccli\e. 

B-3.2.1 If the number of defective chalks found is less than or equal to 
the corresponding number given in col 4 of Table II, the lot shall 
be deemed to have satisfied the dimensidhal requirement for the chalks, 

B-3^ The chalks in the sample shall be weighed in groups of 10 
and each group shall satisfy the requirement in Table I, item (v) 
C see aha A-4J ). 



IS ; 2694 - 1963 

B-3.4 Calcium sulphate content and free moisture content shall be deter* 
mined on a suitable number of chalks after crushing them to the requir- 
ed fineness, as indicated in A-1 and A-2 respectively. Five chalks shall 
be selected from those got according to B-2^ and subjected to transverse 
breaking strength lest separately. 

B-3.4«l A lot shall be declared as conforming to the requirements of 
calcium sulphate, moisture content and transverse breaking strength if 
all the test results obtained a$ under B*3,4 are found satisfactory. 

B*3*5 A lot shall be declared to have met the requirement of the specifi- 
cation if the stipulations laid down in B-3.1 to B-3.4.1 are all fulfilled.
